NewsBrownstein : Margaret Trudeau takes audio route with her hit solo playhttp : **36;11713;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **33;11751;TOOLONG ... title= " " I 'm a mental-health advocate to the core , " Margaret Trudeau says . " alt= " " I 'm a mental-health advocate to the core , " Margaret Trudeau says . " data-portal-copyright= " Dave Sidaway " **28;11786;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1744795 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **33;11816;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was the surprise hit of last summer&amp;rsquo ; s Just for Laughs festival , but Margaret Trudeau&amp;rsquo ; s solo stage show , Certain Woman of An Age , could hardly be classified as Seinfeldian. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; True , Trudeau brought moments of great whimsy , but she also brought more moments of heart-wrenching emotion in three sold-out performances at the Ges&amp;uuml ; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was a compelling and candid , warts and all , confessional in which Trudeau recounted her life-long battle with her demons . Nor did she hold back in recounting her dealings with a Who&amp;rsquo ; s Who of politicos and celebs &amp;mdash ; from Fidel Castro to Ted Kennedy , Mick Jagger to Jack Nicholson &amp;mdash ; she encountered along the way . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You&amp;rsquo ; ll laugh . You&amp;rsquo ; ll cry , &amp;rdquo ; Trudeau had pledged . And , indeed , she left much of the audience doing both . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The show &amp;mdash ; written by Trudeau and Alix Sobler and directed by Kimberly Senior &amp;mdash ; also succeeded on another level : in helping to de-stigmatize mental illness . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trudeau gave only 14 performances of the play , here as well as in Toronto , Chicago and New York . But the good news is that the play was recorded live at New York&amp;rsquo ; s Minetta Lane Theatre and is now available as an audio presentation at &lt;a href= " https : //urldefense.com/v3/http : //audi ... . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;11851;TOOLONG ... title= " " I 'm a mental-health advocate to the core , " Margaret Trudeau says . " alt= " " I 'm a mental-health advocate to the core , " Margaret Trudeau says . " data-portal-copyright= " Dave Sidaway " **28;11886;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1744795 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trudeau has been booked to do three performances of the play at Stratford in June and is also in discussions to take it on a Just for Laughs tour throughout Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m a mental-health advocate to the core , &amp;rdquo ; Trudeau said in a phone interview . &amp;ldquo ; I think everyone who has gone through a mental-health crisis , has sought treatment and has got well , has an obligation to share their hope with what they went through with others . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trudeau is a survivor . Though animated and upbeat now , she went through hell for a long spell . She was committed three times to institutions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her life was hardly Camelot , when as a 23-year-old free spirit she married the 51-year-old , less-free-spirited Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau . She wasn&amp;rsquo ; t prepared for the protocol to come or life with Pierre . &amp;ldquo ; He was a feminist , as long as you weren&amp;rsquo ; t married to him , &amp;rdquo ; she cracks in the play . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Giving birth to her three sons , future prime minister Justin , Sacha and Michel , while in her mid-20s was to precipitate major post-partum depression issues . But it was the tragic death of her youngest son Michel in an avalanche in 1998 that so devastated her and just about did her in. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s one thing for an actor to play the painful life of a stranger , but quite another when it&amp;rsquo ; s the actor&amp;rsquo ; s own painful life being played . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Honestly , I had always wanted to be an actor , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &amp;ldquo ; After my marriage to Pierre was over , I went down to New York to study . I had to go back to Ottawa and raise my three little boys . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I ended up doing more reality TV in a sense , doing interviews . It wasn&amp;rsquo ; t supposed to be acting . But , then again , doing this play isn&amp;rsquo ; t really acting on a certain level , either . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; But actually to get to do this play &amp;hellip ; wow ! &amp;rdquo ; exclaims Trudeau , also the mother of Alicia and Kyle from her second marriage to her ex , Fred Kemper. &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s the real deal . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trudeau gives full credit to director Senior and co-writer Sobler. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; ( Senior ) pushed me , and she pulled me where I needed to be . Trying to have a happy and contributing life is the goal , but depression is the thief that takes you out . As a mania , it causes nothing but damage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Through humour we open another part of our brain . I like to be a bit comedic . Unfortunately my life has been a tragedy as well . I&amp;rsquo ; ve resolved a lot of pain and loss , and I&amp;rsquo ; ve learned that&amp;rsquo ; s life , too . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trudeau was one of the women singled out in the &lt;a href= " https : **33;11916;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Montreal Gazette 's International Women 's Day editorial&lt;/a&gt; last Saturday as someone who has made a difference . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trudeau has found much support for her efforts in dealing with mental illness , both from the public and her kids . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Some of the stories may have been a little shocking to the kids , but they have all listened as I have listened to them . ArtsLocal NewsMontreal moviesNewsMontreal artists in limbo after coronavirus cancellationshttp : **27;13588;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **33;13617;TOOLONG ... title= " Montreal electronic duo Pelada : Chris Vargas ( left ) and Tobias Rochman. " alt= " Montreal electronic duo Pelada : Chris Vargas ( left ) and Tobias Rochman. " data-portal-copyright= " Rebecca Storm " **28;13652;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1746314 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;13682;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; This was supposed to be a breakthrough spring tour in Europe and North America for Montreal-based underground electronic music duo Pelada . Instead , Tobias Rochman and Chris Vargas are stuck in a Brussels hotel , watching show after show get cancelled due to the COVID-19 outbreak . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Major music festivals such as Coachella in California and &lt;a href= " http : **34;13718;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;South by Southwest ( SXSW ) in Texas&lt;/a&gt; have been postponed or cancelled , depriving already financially precarious artists dependent on touring the ability to make ends meet . On Thursday , Montreal &lt;a href= " https : **33;13754;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;promoter Evenko suspended all shows with 250 or more people&lt;/a&gt; for the next 30 days based on measures put in place by the provincial government . The Orchestre symphonique de Montr&amp;eacute ; al ( OSM ) cancelled 11 concerts until April 5 , and their appearance with Kent Nagano at Carnegie Hall in New York March 24 will no longer happen . Popular Montreal indie band Wolf Parade scrapped its upcoming European tour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While major concert promoters and venues are feeling the effects , for many smaller local artists the inability to tour can be career-threatening. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; After six years as a group , this would have been our first profitable tour , &amp;rdquo ; Rochman said Thursday via Skype from Brussels , where they had unexpectedly camped the last three days . &amp;ldquo ; This was our first time working with a more professional agency out of the U.K. We were looking forward to this tour as the first major one after being signed and putting out our record . The shows we&amp;rsquo ; re playing are of a higher profile , with better pay . We&amp;rsquo ; ve been planning for this tour for more than a year . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pelada , who released the critically acclaimed Movimiento Para Cambio in October , were supposed to start the 15-date first leg of their European tour in Italy . That show was cancelled , as was their weekend show in Russia , which required they pay for a work visa upfront . They ended up in Brussels and were due to make their way Friday to Switzerland . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With their shows not going as planned and those expected guarantees &amp;mdash ; normally paid out after the show &amp;mdash ; gone , even an extra $140 for a hotel stay in Belgium can be a financial strain . Flights , trains and buses are other costs bands pay for in advance , and being able to exchange them for a later date isn&amp;rsquo ; t always a help . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Before we came , we applied for P-2 visa work permits for the United States because while we were gone , we needed it to process before our show April 17 at UCLA , &amp;rdquo ; said Vargas. &amp;ldquo ; That was around $2,000 we needed to make sure that was processed while we were here . And it&amp;rsquo ; s not even a guarantee we get the visa . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Added Rochman : &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; d be fine going home , but we don&amp;rsquo ; t even have the means to do that . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The band was set to play high-profile festivals like Primavera in Spain and Rewire in the Netherlands . With a touring itinerary set to last through the summer , Rochman and Vargas left their day jobs to pursue music full-time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When you&amp;rsquo ; re living right on the threshold of profitability , it can be very dangerous , &amp;rdquo ; said Rochman. &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re in the gig economy , and the reality of seeing that bubble burst is devastating . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Micha&amp;euml ; l Bardier books and manages local and international artists with his Montreal company Heavy Trip . He estimates he&amp;rsquo ; s lost $250,000 in guarantees for his acts so far , in addition to flights and other costs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Honestly , the company has been in a good position lately . We&amp;rsquo ; ve been booking bigger tours in the U.S. and Europe , &amp;rdquo ; Bardier said . &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re not going to put the key in the door , but for sure , this is rough . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; An added problem for Bardier and many others is bands route their tours around major North American festivals in the spring such as SXSW , Big Ears in Nashville and Mission Creek Festival in Iowa . All three have been cancelled . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Honestly , it&amp;rsquo ; s just really bad timing because last year around this time , I really determined March and April to be a really good period for international , experimental , world and jazz to tour in North America , so I really gave everything I had to route these tours , &amp;rdquo ; Bardier said . The protagonists " almost all have ties to various West Indian backgrounds and places , " the Montreal author says , " but one of the things that grounds ( the book ) is that all of the main characters are Canadians . " " data-portal-copyright= " Allen McInnis " **28;14014;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1744809 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Kaie Kellough might have been a musician but for the fact that , like many of us , he found it harder than expected . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " I got acquainted with frustration , " the soft-spoken Montreal writer recalled of his early attempts at learning musical instruments . " It 's that realization that you ca n't just do something the way you want to do it , you have to follow a particular technique . You train yourself to the instrument , because the instrument wo n't adapt to you . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Stymied though he might have been by the violin , Kellough did n't give up on the idea of artistic expression . On moving to Montreal from Calgary in the late 1990s , the Vancouver-born son of mixed Guyanese parents soon found a supportive community in the local spoken-word scene -- where he did , in fact , find himself in numerous cross-disciplinary collaborations with musicians of various kinds . But it was in literature that he eventually found his true m ? tier . His 2016 debut novel Accord ? on , shortlisted for the Amazon Canada First Novel Award , was an experimental/satirical tour-de-force that announced the arrival of a major new Canadian voice ; last year 's Magnetic Equator was shortlisted for the QWF 's A.M. Klein Prize for Poetry . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Now , expanding Kellough 's remit further still , comes &lt;a href= " https : //kaie.ca/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Dominoes at the Crossroads&lt;/a&gt; ( V ? hicule Press , 208 pages , $19.95 ) . An interwoven set of 12 stories occupying the fecund zone where memoir , fiction and essay meet , it 's a prismatic , lyrical , free-ranging , genre-fluid work that ends up functioning as a sort of cross-Canada travelogue of the Caribbean diaspora . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " They almost all have ties to various West Indian backgrounds and places -- Haiti , Guyana , St. Vincent , " Kellough said of his protagonists . " But one of the things that grounds ( the book ) is that all of the main characters are Canadians . The Canadian side of their identities is foregrounded ; their origins form a kind of ambient backdrop . It 's their experience working the intersection of Canadian culture and the identity they 've been brought up with that really interested me. " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;When it 's suggested that the book is marked by a deep sense of identification with his characters , Kellough readily concurs . " Sure . Having grown up with those ties , these are in a way portraits of people I 've always known , that I 've dated and had friendships with over the years . Writing about them is second nature to me. " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;14044;TOOLONG ... title= " Kaie Kellough says his mission statement is " to find a vocabulary for my experience " as a mixed-race Caribbean-Canadian. " alt= " Kaie Kellough says his mission statement is " to find a vocabulary for my experience " as a mixed-race Caribbean-Canadian. " data-portal-copyright= " Allen McInnis " **28;14079;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1744790 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Music -- there 's that subject again -- is a major unifying thread in a book that , in less sure hands , might have spun off in a few directions too many . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " I wanted it to take place in different parts of Canada , and for there to be a constant sense of displacement , " Kellough said . " The setting of the story is never rooted and fixed , and I found the travelling musician a good metaphor for that . When you 're touring , you hit places in a superficial way -- you get a quick glimpse and a brief experience , and then you 're on to the next one . In a way it 's a fugitive existence , reflective of migrations and marooning , but also reflective of the progress of some kinds of improvised music . In a solo you 'll depart from the main melodic progression and eventually return to it . You 're never completely arriving . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;A Kellough story , while roughly incorporating the standard beginning , middle and end of narrative tradition , will often jump through holes in the time-space continuum . Historical figures like 18th-century firebrand Marie-Joseph Ang ? lique , who may or may not have deliberately burned down the colonial-era Old Port ( " It was an act of resistance that I 'd like to see commemorated , " said Kellough ) , and modern-day episodes like the &lt;a href= " https : **33;14109;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;1969 Sir George Williams occupation&lt;/a&gt; by Caribbean students ( " I do n't think it 's been properly historicized . Those events were remarkable , to say the least . They transformed people 's lives . They were part of a radical moment . " ) are illuminated through recontextualization . A minor Senegalese character in Hubert Aquin 's Next Episode is transposed to an underground hallway in Peel m ? tro station in a story inspired by a real-life African import shop . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " When someplace like that shop has been around for as long as it has , it becomes part of the imagination of the city , " Kellough said . " It gets embedded in the way we think of the place . " &lt;span class= " Apple-converted-space " &gt; **26;14144;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Investing otherwise overlooked figures with the dignity of literary attention is a Kellough hallmark ; another is his knack of shifting the perspective on a familiar subject in a way that shows it in a revelatory new light . One such case in the new book is Jack Kerouac 's On the Road , the generation-defining novel of Americans in search of their own country . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " In a book where so many people are on the road , I thought it would be fun to have that book make its cameo , " Kellough said . But there 's more to it than fun . The narrator of Petit Marronage , on reading Kerouac 's cult classic as an adult , is disappointed by the realization that its footloose white seekers " had free passage wherever they wanted . I wanted the narrator and Dean Moriarty to experience limitation , real life , to attempt to cross a border that they could not cross . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;A pertinent question to pose of a writer whose instincts have already led him to so many places and forms is that of driving principle . Does Kellough have an overarching mission statement ? &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " Yes , I do , " he said without hesitation . " It 's to find a vocabulary for my experience . When I was growing up in the ' 70s and ' 80s in Western Canada , there was the official rhetoric of multiculturalism that talked about how the state wanted to approach the existence in Canada of people like me and my parents . But it did n't say anything about what my experience , and the experience of other mixed-race Caribbean-Canadians , was actually like here . It was invisible . And when you 're invisible in the culture at large , one of the things you 're required to do is create your presence , and literature is my platform to do that . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " It 's not a question just of representation . It 's deeper than that . It 's a question of actual existence . But is the big party equally accessible to all ? Is the demographic often referred to as " of a certain age " -- for convenience 's sake , let 's define it as those born during or prior to the Diefenbaker administration -- being subtly shunted out ? ( The recent &lt;a href= " https : **33;17513;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Nuit Blanche&lt;/a&gt; is an outlier here , with any practical challenges more than forgivable in light of the unique concept. ) &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;It 's not a matter of wanting to dictate the terms . No , it 's more a question of having some basic needs acknowledged . We like to get a good night 's sleep . We like to have the option of sitting down once in a while . Is that so much to ask ? Herewith , then , some suggestions to those who run the show . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3 class= " p1 " &gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Start on **28;17548;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;It 's hard not to feel there 's some sort of class-based bias at play here . When you go to , say , the opera , you can be secure in knowing the show will start at the advertised time , or very close to it . So why is it acceptable for small-venue alternative music events to start egregiously late , and without so much as an onstage apology ? ( Yes , indie rock , I 'm looking mostly at you here . ) As my mother would say to me when I showed up late for family dinners , that 's just bad manners . Moreover , it 's a practice that serves as built-in discouragement to those elders among us who might still feel inclined to investigate the scene now and then . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3 class= " p1 " &gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Do n't have multiple opening **28;17578;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;It 's only asking for trouble . As for staking out a space at the front , the last time I was willing to do that was for Kraftwerk at Metropolis in 2014 , and that was because they were Kraftwerk . Soberingly , I recently found that even leaning against a counter for three-plus hours -- at a Vampire Weekend show in the same venue , the balcony seats being full and the floor being crammed with tall young people -- was exhausting . " data-portal-copyright= " Tim Snow " **28;19733;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1733682 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;19763;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nuit Blanche is a concept tailor-made for Montreal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Back in 1989 , the Helsinki Festival kicked off something called Night of the Arts , a similar idea in which folks could check out museums , art galleries and bookstores in a single night . Nuit Blanche came to life in 2002 in Paris , and once again the focus was on contemporary art . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nuit Blanche began here in 2003 , and organizers gave it a unique Montreal twist . Like events in Helsinki , Paris and some 120 other cities around the world , our Nuit Blanche has a contemporary art component , but there is much more to the all-night event here . It features a wide array of cultural genres , notably music , virtual-reality installations and standup comedy . Because it&amp;rsquo ; s Montreal , the bottom line is that it&amp;rsquo ; s one big party &amp;mdash ; and better yet , almost everything is free . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We really adapted La Nuit Blanche to the spirit of Montreal , &amp;rdquo ; said Laurent Saulnier , vice-president of programming at L&amp;rsquo ; &amp;Eacute ; quipe Spectra , which organizes the event . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The spirit of Montreal is all about partying , let&amp;rsquo ; s admit it , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; People here like to party , especially by the end of February , when it&amp;rsquo ; s been a couple of months of days getting dark too early , Arctic cold , etc. , etc . People want to go out . So we give people the perfect excuse to go out &amp;mdash ; a wide variety of activities in all sorts of different places , and the vast majority of them are free of charge . It&amp;rsquo ; s pretty cool . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This year&amp;rsquo ; s Nuit Blanche takes control of the city centre Saturday night into Sunday morning . You can sample an astonishing amount of culture &amp;mdash ; everything from electronic-music DJs Tokimonsta and Whipped Cream at Place des Festivals to Canadian paintings from the 1980s at the Mus&amp;eacute ; e d&amp;rsquo ; art contemporain , a virtual-reality adaptation of Franz Kafka&amp;rsquo ; s terrifying novella The Metamorphosis at the Goethe-Institut , and drag queens performing out on the street in the Gay Village . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; La Nuit Blanche is for me a very big , very open menu from which you can choose whatever tempts you , &amp;rdquo ; said Saulnier . &amp;ldquo ; There are loads of people , for example , who use La Nuit Blanche to move their bodies , because there are places where you can skate and do other sports . For others , La Nuit Blanche is all about the joy of going to a museum at midnight and discovering the museum at an unusual time of day . For some , La Nuit Blanche is simply synonymous with the word &amp;lsquo ; party . &amp;rsquo ; &amp;hellip ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a menu where absolutely everything is possible . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;19799;TOOLONG ... title= " Nuit Blanche 's outdoor site featured a dance floor in 2015 . As well as Joan Crawford and Bolshoi giant Maya Plisetskaya , he mentioned such high-energy comedians as Lucille Ball , Phyllis Diller , Gracie Allen and Joan Rivers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I send videos to the guys and I say , &amp;lsquo ; Please look at the way they use their eyes and their facial expressions , and even the way they tip their heads , &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; said Dobrin. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Trocks , as they&amp;rsquo ; re affectionately known , were launched in New York in 1974 , part of a more assertive push for LGBTQ visibility in the after-effects of the Stonewall riots . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What began as a late-night lark in off-off-Broadway venues soon blossomed into a truly spectacular hothouse flower . They&amp;rsquo ; ve performed with Shirley MacLaine , had think pieces written about them in publications such as the New Yorker and New York Times , and were snapped for a photo essay in Vogue . Now an international brand , they were the subject of the film Rebels on Pointe , which was nominated in a documentary category at the 2019 Canadian Screen Awards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re almost 50 years old now , which kind of speaks for itself , &amp;rdquo ; said Dobrin , who joined as a dancer in 1980. &amp;ldquo ; We have staying power . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gender politics have obviously undergone major changes since the Trocks first jet&amp;eacute ; d onto the scene , but Dobrin argues the troupe is still very much a progressive force . &amp;ldquo ; When you talk about drag and its place in society , a lot of times it&amp;rsquo ; s used to highlight the absurdities and inconsistencies of gender stereotypes . We&amp;rsquo ; ve definitely always played with that . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As an example , Dobrin points to the Trocks&amp;rsquo ; treatment of Swan Lake . &amp;ldquo ; Usually the Swan Queen is very vulnerable , while the prince is all strong and macho . We do it the other way around . ArtsLocal NewsMontreal theatreTheatre : Hit thriller La Meute becomes a snarling Mob at Centaurhttp : **33;21411;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **33;21446;TOOLONG ... title= " While the dynamic plotting of Mob is full of carefully calibrated surprises , playwright Catherine-Anne Toupin acknowledges the main theme : " We 're all becoming desensitized to a lack of empathy and understanding for somebody who 's different . " " alt= " While the dynamic plotting of Mob is full of carefully calibrated surprises , playwright Catherine-Anne Toupin acknowledges the main theme : " We 're all becoming desensitized to a lack of empathy and understanding for somebody who 's different . " " data-portal-copyright= " John Mahoney " **28;21481;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1734127 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Playwright Catherine-Anne Toupin likes to make her audiences gasp with shock and awe . She has heard those gratifying gasps many times over the last two years while performing in her own twisting , turning thriller La Meute , which opens at the Centaur on Tuesday in an English version called Mob . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Every single night , there were two moments especially when I heard people saying &amp;lsquo ; oh my god ! &amp;rsquo ; very loudly , &amp;rdquo ; recalled Toupin. &amp;ldquo ; Which I love . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; La Meute was first produced in 2018 at La Licorne , which is where Toupin joined the Montreal Gazette for a chat . Such was the enormous buzz the play created that it was reprised twice , both times selling out well in advance of opening night . Centaur artistic director Eda Holmes was at the premi&amp;egrave ; re , immediately collared Toupin as she came off stage shaking with nervous energy , and offered there and then to put it on at the Centaur . The English version&amp;rsquo ; s run has already been extended by a week due to popular demand . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No doubt part of the attraction of the play has been the dynamic plotting , which sees a woman named Sophie taking to the road after a work-related trauma . She winds up at a remote bed-and-breakfast run by a deceptively nice young man and his elderly relative . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Already you might have the screeching violins of a certain movie thriller playing in your head , and you wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t be far off the mark . Although Toupin says the similarities in those opening scenes to the plot of Psycho are entirely accidental , she fesses up to being steeped in the language , mood and hairpin twists of classic edge-of-the-seat films . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was introduced to them by my wonderful grandma , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; She loved old movies and she was the official babysitter to me and my sister , and we only watched old movies together . So that&amp;rsquo ; s where I discovered the likes of Hitchcock and Otto Preminger . I was probably 12 when I saw Psycho for the first time &amp;mdash ; too young ! But I really enjoyed it . So Hitchcock especially has , I think without my knowing it , had a huge influence on my writing . I&amp;rsquo ; ve seen all his movies at least 20 times . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Exactly where Mob goes after that intriguing opening is something we can&amp;rsquo ; t discuss here if we&amp;rsquo ; re to preserve its carefully calibrated surprises . Suffice to say the play&amp;rsquo ; s themes revolve around misogyny in the workplace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think what&amp;rsquo ; s relevant is the violence between the characters , &amp;rdquo ; said Toupin , with practised avoidance of spilling too many beans . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s really about how they get into that vicious circle and can&amp;rsquo ; t get themselves out of it . I think we&amp;rsquo ; re all becoming desensitized to a lack of empathy and understanding for somebody who&amp;rsquo ; s different . That&amp;rsquo ; s the main subject of the play . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The misogyny angle has clearly struck a chord in the #MeToo era , and the exact nature of&amp;nbsp ; Sophie&amp;rsquo ; s workplace ( we have to keep that under wraps , too ) is arguably central to the powerful effect of the play . But at the end of the day , said Toupin , &amp;ldquo ; to me it has no importance which industry this play takes place in . It could take place in the film industry , it could take place in a restaurant . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; ( For the record , the play has nothing to do with the Qu&amp;eacute ; b&amp;eacute ; cois far-right group that goes by the name La Meute . Toupin began writing it well before that ugly development in the province&amp;rsquo ; s politics. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;21511;TOOLONG ... title= " Catherine-Anne Toupin at La Licorne , where her play La Meute -- about trauma and misogyny , set in a remote B&amp;B -- sold out three times over . " alt= " Catherine-Anne Toupin at La Licorne , where her play La Meute -- about trauma and misogyny , set in a remote B&amp;B -- sold out three times over . " data-portal-copyright= " John Mahoney " **28;21546;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1734126 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; As well as the promise of a gripping night out , La Meute had another ace up its sleeve when it played La Licorne : the onstage appearance of Toupin herself . She&amp;rsquo ; s a household name among francophone Quebecers , thanks to her television appearances in the prison drama Unit&amp;eacute ; 9 , Les hauts et les bas de Sophie Paquin and in the sitcom Boomerang , which she also created . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Born in 1975 in Ottawa , where her father worked in the federal government , Toupin soon moved to Quebec City after her father got a job in the provincial government . She came to Montreal in 1996 when she enrolled at the Conservatoire de musique et d&amp;rsquo ; art dramatique , after which she started Th&amp;eacute ; &amp;acirc ; tre ni plus ni moins with Fr&amp;eacute ; d&amp;eacute ; ric Blanchette and Fran&amp;ccedil ; ois L&amp;eacute ; tourneau , both now major figures on Montreal&amp;rsquo ; s francophone theatre scene . That company&amp;rsquo ; s first production was Toupin&amp;rsquo ; s L&amp;rsquo ; Envie , which she also acted in , and which played at Th&amp;eacute ; &amp;acirc ; tre d&amp;rsquo ; Aujourd&amp;rsquo ; hui in 2004. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Toupin cites Harold Pinter as one of her favourite playwrights , and you can see his influence in her second play , &amp;Agrave ; pr&amp;eacute ; sent , which premi&amp;egrave ; red at La Licorne in 2007 . It&amp;rsquo ; s a superb tragicomic domestic nightmare with distinct similarities to Pinter&amp;rsquo ; s The Homecoming . Unaccountably , no anglo theatre in Montreal , or indeed in Canada , has picked it up &amp;mdash ; it had to travel to Bath in the U.K. to play in English , as Right Now . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All the francophone first runs of Toupin&amp;rsquo ; s plays have seen her taking the lead female role . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s important for me , when I&amp;rsquo ; ve written something , to perform it for the first time , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; I find that&amp;rsquo ; s part of the arc of creation . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She speaks flawless English , so I wondered aloud why she isn&amp;rsquo ; t again putting herself into Sophie&amp;rsquo ; s shoes for this Centaur production . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Oh , I&amp;rsquo ; ve already performed it 80 times , &amp;rdquo ; she laughed , with a dismissive wave , before expressing confidence in the play&amp;rsquo ; s new Sophie , Adrianne Richards , as well as with Richards&amp;rsquo ; s co-stars , Matthew Kabwe and Susan Bain . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As with Right Now , this English version is by Chris Campbell , a British translator who was literary manager in London&amp;rsquo ; s prestigious Royal Court Theatre . Toupin reckons director Andrew Shaver will keep the play grounded in a Canadian milieu . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of seeing her work make the leap across the linguistic divide , Toupin said : &amp;ldquo ; I actually find translation exciting . You lose something , but gain something else . I think the biggest challenge in the English translation has been to find the poetry of the violence . &amp;hellip ; It feels like a kind of a dream place that the characters enter , and I want the audience to enter into that too &amp;mdash ; to be appalled , but also strangely compelled . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And , of course , to yell &amp;ldquo ; oh my god ! &amp;rdquo ; in all the right places . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;AT A GLANCE&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **42;21576;TOOLONG plays from Tuesday , March 3 through Sunday , March 29 at Centaur Theatre , 453 S&lt;/em&gt; &lt;em&gt;t-Fran ? ois-Xavier St. Tickets : $44 to $56 ; under-30s and students $30 ; seniors $40 to $46 . The DJ played Canadian pop music , including Shania Twain and Len . ( Remember Len ? ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Well , OK , the Canadian Embassy threw the party . But as Canada&amp;rsquo ; s ambassador to Germany and special envoy to the European Union , that made it Dion&amp;rsquo ; s party . And though Dion is not exactly a party guy , he was rolling with it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Based out of Germany&amp;rsquo ; s hippest city , the former leader of the Liberal Party is enjoying life after partisan politics . And he&amp;rsquo ; s enjoying Berlin &amp;mdash ; perhaps not as you or I might enjoy Berlin , but he&amp;rsquo ; s enjoying it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I am not aware of any diplomat from any country unhappy to be in Berlin , &amp;rdquo ; Dion said in an interview at the Canadian Embassy on Monday morning . &amp;ldquo ; The city itself is very enjoyable . It&amp;rsquo ; s still affordable . Traffic is a bit difficult , but if you compare it even with Munich , it&amp;rsquo ; s much better . The cuisine &amp;mdash ; I will not make any faux pas about German cuisine , but it&amp;rsquo ; s universal here . You have all the styles of restaurant you want . There are more museums than you&amp;rsquo ; ll have time to visit . And a lot of green spaces . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Green spaces are important to Dion , a renowned environmentalist and former environment minister . ( Again with the jokes ! ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On that note , Saturday&amp;rsquo ; s party was a celebration of this year&amp;rsquo ; s substantial Canadian presence at the Berlinale ( a.k.a. the Berlin International Film Festival ) . Between the two , with all the different cultural programming selected , it&amp;rsquo ; s really formidable . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;22111;TOOLONG ... title= " Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and Quebec author Kim Th ? y talk about migration and diversity at the Munich Security Conference this month . " data-portal-copyright= " Canadian Embassy " **28;22146;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1733310 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Those thinking all this is a little outside Dion&amp;rsquo ; s wheelhouse may be forgetting that when he was leader of the opposition , he was also the spokesperson for the Liberals on heritage and culture . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Seeing Canada accept the invitation from the Frankfurt Book Fair brings him satisfaction , as he watched the Harper government decline the same opportunity in 2014 &amp;mdash ; a decision he criticized at the time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I said , &amp;lsquo ; We need to say the book fair is something we will support&amp;rsquo ; &amp;mdash ; and once elected , we did it . " data-portal-copyright= " Bertrand Calmeau " **28;23547;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1732229 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; BERLIN &amp;mdash ; The duo of Fran&amp;ccedil ; ois L&amp;eacute ; tourneau and Jean-Fran&amp;ccedil ; ois Rivard are no longer Quebec&amp;rsquo ; s best-kept secret . The creators of the hit TV series Les Invincibles and &lt;a href= " https : **33;23577;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;S ? rie noire&lt;/a&gt; premi&amp;egrave ; red their new show C&amp;rsquo ; est comme &amp;ccedil ; a que je t&amp;rsquo ; aime ( Happily Married ) Tuesday evening at the 70th Berlinale &amp;mdash ; a.k.a. the Berlin International Film Festival &amp;mdash ; where they are in select company . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In its sixth year , the Berlinale Series section highlights just eight TV and streaming programs from around the globe , with adventurous new works by Cate Blanchett , &lt;a href= " https : **33;23612;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Damien Chazelle&lt;/a&gt; , Jason Segel and &lt;a href= " https : **33;23647;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Greece 's Athina Rachel Tsangari&lt;/a&gt; , among others . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; As we said last night , &amp;lsquo ; Qui l&amp;rsquo ; e&amp;ucirc ; t cru ? &amp;rsquo ; ( Who would have thought ? ) , &amp;rdquo ; said director Rivard. &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a nice pat on the back . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In TV , there are no premi&amp;egrave ; res , &amp;rdquo ; added writer-actor L&amp;eacute ; tourneau. &amp;ldquo ; This is validation . It&amp;rsquo ; s good for the ego &amp;hellip ; ( and ) it&amp;rsquo ; s an interesting spotlight . We had no international ambitions , but if the show can get outside of Quebec and intrigue people , great . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Imbued with the same quirkiness , visual sophistication and deadpan humour of their previous productions , C&amp;rsquo ; est comme &amp;ccedil ; a que je t&amp;rsquo ; aime follows the wildly unpredictable antics of two couples &amp;mdash ; Huguette and Ga&amp;eacute ; tan , Serge and Micheline &amp;mdash ; in the Quebec City suburb of Ste-Foy in 1974 . Their relationships are thrown into disarray when their kids go off to summer camp for three weeks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;23682;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;23717;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; The first two episodes of the series were shown at the Berlinale . A shrewd bit of foreshadowing at the beginning of the first episode offers a teaser as to where the seemingly innocuous plot might be headed : the two couples are found floating naked , face down in a backyard pool , and are subsequently described as &amp;ldquo ; the worst criminals in the history of organized crime in the Quebec City region&amp;rdquo ; in the &amp;rsquo ; 70s . It&amp;rsquo ; s more funny than scary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We like the unpredictable , &amp;rdquo ; Rivard said . &amp;ldquo ; When we write a story , we try to give audiences something they don&amp;rsquo ; t expect . If you know what&amp;rsquo ; s coming , it gets boring fast . We like to keep people destabilized . It motivates you to keep watching . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The offbeat , incongruous aspect makes it so that if you just watched the first and the 10th episode , you would be like , &amp;lsquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not the same series , &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; L&amp;eacute ; tourneau said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Not that it&amp;rsquo ; s not the same series , &amp;rdquo ; Rivard countered , &amp;ldquo ; but you will have missed some things . A lot happens . Each episode has its peculiarities , and leads to the next , like dominoes . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That ability to surprise has made L&amp;eacute ; tourneau and Rivard&amp;rsquo ; s projects stand out on the Quebec television landscape , and is now bringing them around the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Berlinale Series&amp;rsquo ; new section director , Julia Fidel , was impressed by the self-contained universe the pair created , and the diverse cultural comparisons that can be made . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The show &amp;ldquo ; constructs an entire world of its own with black humour and 1970s interiors , &amp;rdquo ; she says in &lt;a href= " https : **33;23753;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;an interview published on the Berlinale website&lt;/a&gt; . &amp;ldquo ; It reminds me of John Updike&amp;rsquo ; s novel Couples . He was inspired by events in his personal life &amp;mdash ; some from his childhood , and some from the more recent past . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My girlfriend and I brought our kid to summer camp , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; He was eight years old , and we were nervous to be without him . Island GazetteMystic Toolkit tackles esoteric elements in contemporary pop culturehttp : **33;24888;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **33;24923;TOOLONG ... title= " The Mystic Toolkit exhibit runs until March 8 at Stewart Hall Art Gallery , Pointe-Claire . " data-portal-copyright= " Alexis Bellavance " **28;24958;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1728447 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The exhibition Mystic Toolkit , ongoing at Stewart Hall , is an artistic inquiry into what curator Ana&amp;iuml ; s Castro sees as an interesting trend among &lt;a href= " https : **33;24988;TOOLONG ... . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One of the things I&amp;rsquo ; ve noticed is people in my generation are incredibly interested in alternative spiritual practices that were very popular in the &amp;rsquo ; 70s , and that are now resurging with a vengeance , &amp;rdquo ; said Castro . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mystic Toolkit includes game table installations by OMSK Social Club , a Berlin-based artist whose work lies at the intersection of art , LARP ( live action role-play ) , and RGP ( real game play ) ; as well as the intricate stitched works of intersecting circles by Isa Carrillo , a Mexican artist who is interested in the hidden and invisible phenomena inherent in everyday life . These works , along with others by Alex Coma , Hector Jimenez Castillo , Marigold Santos and Jennifer Murphy , speak to the theme of mystic connection central to the show . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The qualities of contemplation and surrender , shared by mystics and the artists in this exhibition , are meant to be a reflection of an interest in the deeper invisible connections of existence . All of the artists are working at a time when climate change , spirituality rather than organized religion , and the challenges of hope in the face of rising political tensions , are bringing many of the issues from the &amp;rsquo ; 70s full circle , calling out for attention once more , Castro noted . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jennifer Murphy&amp;rsquo ; s work &amp;lsquo ; The Shadow of Sirius&amp;rsquo ; lies in the centre of the gallery . On a raised circle covered with soil , a spiral of seashells swirls outward from the centre , echoing the spiral inherent in the form of each individual shell . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What interested me in Jennifer&amp;rsquo ; s piece was how it captures the idea of rotation of the earth , rotation around the sun , and the solar system and the infinite rotation of the universe , &amp;rdquo ; said Castro . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Murphy said that her work is &amp;ldquo ; about ecology and loss&amp;rdquo ; , and much of her work comes from what she calls the &amp;ldquo ; assemblage&amp;rdquo ; of different things she collects. &amp;ldquo ; Being a collector is like being a hunter , and the chance and surprise of stumbling on something is part of what inspires me , &amp;rdquo ; she added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The shells in &amp;lsquo ; The Shadow of Sirius&amp;rsquo ; come from a collection of 1,500 shells from around the world that a woman in Ontario collected and logged throughout her life . When she died , her son put the collection in an online auction and Murphy bought it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As one stands looking at the spiral , or walks slowly around the work , one is witness to a collection that includes species that are now extinct . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I could tell by the logbook , that this was an elegy to what we&amp;rsquo ; re losing on the planet , &amp;rdquo ; said Murphy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alluding to the poetic form similar to a eulogy , Murphy invites viewers to contemplate the swirl of memory , time , and connection , and like the generation before them that pondered similar questions , this present generation of art makers contemplates what the future may hold for them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This work is also about loss , coupled with the fantastical , beauty and hope , &amp;rdquo ; said Murphy . &amp;ldquo ; Everyone is looking for a different way of being in the world , and asking different questions in different ways . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; An art show conceived for people who remember the promise of an age of Aquarius , when &amp;ldquo ; peace will guide the planet and love will steer the stars&amp;rdquo ; , as well as for an audience of millennials , both will see their common concerns expressed in the art selected by Castro . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mystic Toolkit runs until March 8 at Stewart Hall Art Gallery , 176 Lakeshore Dr , Pointe-Claire. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;25023;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;25065;TOOLONG ... season of love -- eccentric , unmitigated , sour and soul -- is coming to **27;25100;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;25129;TOOLONG ... cradle linked two schools and four **32;25164;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;25198;TOOLONG ... Set in the cellphone- and internet-free bubble of the 1990s , it&amp;rsquo ; s a raw coming-of-age story the likes of which we rarely see on the big screen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The film crashed through the sold-out Urania Berlin e.V . theatre like a tidal wave Saturday , sweeping up all in attendance and carrying them out to sea . Most impressive is that , as its name suggests , the festival&amp;rsquo ; s Generation 14plus section is geared to young film fans , 14 and up . There were viewers of all ages in attendance , including many teens , attending with friends or family . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was completely conscious , during the screening , of the adolescents discovering it , &amp;rdquo ; Barbeau-Lavalette said . &amp;ldquo ; It wasn&amp;rsquo ; t just adolescents , but I knew there were some , and to feel the reactions of these people at this turning point in their life &amp;mdash ; to hear them laugh , cry and reacting to the strong moments I had hoped for &amp;mdash ; it was touching . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The scariest thing for me was wondering whether the emotions would travel across borders , but there was something palpable in the room . Catherine&amp;rsquo ; s adolescence could easily be that of a young Berliner . From ( the moment I realized that ) , I knew the film could go anywhere . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;25541;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;25577;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Carrying the movie is a fearless performance by Depeault , who at Saturday&amp;rsquo ; s premiere exhibited the same combination of spontaneity and charisma as her character , twirling giddily as the cast and crew made their entrance , just before the movie began . It was very emotional . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Barbeau-Lavalette has been to the Berlinale twice before , with Le Ring and &lt;a href= " https : **33;25613;TOOLONG ... , both films with socio-political subtexts . " " data-portal-copyright= " Pierre Obendrauf " **28;25922;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1727696 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;25952;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; During Rebecca Foon&amp;rsquo ; s first year in Montreal , back in 1996-97 , she would sometimes take a break from her studies at McGill to go play her cello at the corner of St-Laurent Blvd. and Prince Arthur St. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One day a homeless man stopped in his tracks and began to listen . He dropped to his knees , enrapt , where he remained for the next 15 minutes . He finally stood up , walked over to her open cello case and emptied his pockets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I felt so bad , but also so moved , &amp;rdquo ; Foon said , recalling that moment more than 20 years ago . &amp;ldquo ; I was like , &amp;lsquo ; Wow , music is powerful . &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She never returned to perform on that corner , but she has gone on to create powerful moments , and movements , both on stage and in the global fight against climate change . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;25988;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;As co-founder of Pathway to Paris&lt;/a&gt; , a non-profit organization devoted to raising awareness about the urgency of climate action , she has rubbed shoulders with rock stars , activists , academics and politicians including Patti Smith , Thom Yorke , Naomi Klein , Michael Stipe , Cat Power , Flea and Talib Kweli , some of whom have become her friends . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She is a former member of Montreal post-rock bands Thee Silver Mt . Zion Memorial Orchestra and Esmerine ( which won a Juno for best instrumental album in 2014 ) , and has put out two evocative &lt;a href= " https : **33;26023;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;solo projects under the name Saltland&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This week Foon released Waxing Moon , her first album under her own name . Although it doesn&amp;rsquo ; t address climate change directly , the song cycle expresses the overwhelming feeling of being a human facing extinction . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This album is very intimate for me , &amp;rdquo ; Foon said over tea on a snowed-in afternoon at her Rosemont home . &amp;ldquo ; I was exploring things I never had before , such as playing piano and singing &amp;mdash ; and the singing is much more raw and open . It just felt like the right moment to use my own name . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;26058;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;26093;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Though she describes this as her most song-based album , Foon doesn&amp;rsquo ; t make songs so much as soundscapes &amp;mdash ; stirring , emotionally loaded environments that envelop you , casting a spell that makes you forget what time it is , what day it is , where you are and what you were doing . That said , she approached this project with a sense of purpose . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I just can&amp;rsquo ; t make love songs right now , &amp;rdquo ; she said , while admitting this is partly a heartbreak album . &amp;ldquo ; I need to be talking and using music as a platform to talk about what&amp;rsquo ; s going on , and doing everything I can , with my limited capacity as a human , to fight for our planet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; So this album is a more spiritual album . There&amp;rsquo ; s more to life than just this physical plane and reality . It&amp;rsquo ; s tapping into that . It&amp;rsquo ; s also just talking about a feeling of awakeness , and from that comes a hope for transformation . " " data-portal-copyright= " Pierre Obendrauf " **28;26234;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1727696 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;26264;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;During POP Montreal in September&lt;/a&gt; , Foon brought her enhanced sensitivity to the mix as she and sax behemoth Colin Stetson joined legendary American avant-garde artist Laurie Anderson at the Rialto Theatre . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She lives for such moments . She has been struck by the genuine sense of commitment from those offering to lend their name , ideas and artistry to the cause . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m just so moved by the compassion , and people truly caring about our planet and wanting to use their music as a platform for change , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; I find that deeply essential and inspiring right now . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re in a state of emergency . Joseph Matheson and Louise Pitre deliver a wealth of ' 60s protest music by songwriters of Jewish heritage in The Times They Are A Changin ' . " " data-portal-copyright= " Joanna Akyol " **28;26947;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1728176 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The sound of silence gives way to the sounds of the &amp;rsquo ; 60s at the Segal next week , as a musical show starring husband-and-wife team Louise Pitre and W. Joseph Matheson moves in just as the silent-retreat drama &lt;a href= " https : **33;26977;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Small Mouth Sounds&lt;/a&gt; moves out . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Times They Are A Changin&amp;rsquo ; , which plays from March 1 to 22 , and which originated at Toronto&amp;rsquo ; s Harold Green Jewish Theatre Company in 2017 , is a celebration of protest songs from songwriters of Jewish heritage such as Carole King , Paul Simon , Mama Cass , Arlo Guthrie and , of course , Bob Dylan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Segal audiences will still have searing memories of four-time Dora Award-winning Pitre&amp;rsquo ; s astonishing portrayal of &lt;a href= " https : **33;27012;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt; ? dith Piaf in The Angel and the Sparrow&lt;/a&gt; a couple of years ago . That show also featured Matheson , as most of the men in Piaf&amp;rsquo ; s life . The two also performed together in Could You Wait ? , a musical written by Matheson based on the wartime romance between his parents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But The Times They Are A Changin&amp;rsquo ; offers more than a stage reunion featuring fondly remembered hits expertly sung . The songs have been carefully chosen to run the gamut from &amp;lsquo ; 60s idealism to disillusionment and anger . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Says Pitre , joining Matheson on a phone call with the Montreal Gazette : &amp;ldquo ; When the Harold Green theatre asked us to create the show , and when Joe and I got to researching , I think what surprised us the most was how heartbreaking it was that a lot of these songs could have been written today &amp;mdash ; that they still apply . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Matheson agrees that some of the content &amp;ldquo ; can be a bit more sombre than how people expect , &amp;rdquo ; but adds &amp;ldquo ; we still feel there&amp;rsquo ; s a lot of hope&amp;rdquo ; in the show . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In addition to a five-piece band , Pitre and Matheson will be accompanied by video imagery from Dan Bowman. &amp;ldquo ; We really felt we didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to just stand there singing songs , &amp;rdquo ; says Pitre. &amp;ldquo ; So there&amp;rsquo ; s a fair bit of video , which is a huge part of the show . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That became our accessory , &amp;rdquo ; says Matheson , &amp;ldquo ; in the sense that we could sing what everybody thinks is a lovely , hopeful song , but the video shows you the other side . ( You get ) what could have been and where we actually are . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Summing up a decade&amp;rsquo ; s worth of classic protest songs in 90 minutes naturally presented a logistical challenge for Pitre and Matheson . Inevitably , many favourites fell by the wayside . For Pitre , the most painful omission was Simon and Garfunkel&amp;rsquo ; s The Boxer . But the choices they made are by no means obvious ones . I confess I had to Google the three songs Pitre cites as the ones she feels most encapsulate the themes of the show ( One Tin Soldier , Last Night I Had the Strangest Dream and Save the Country ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As the show arrives at the Segal , one question that might be on an audience&amp;rsquo ; s mind is how many songs , if any , are we going to get from the rich catalogue of Montreal&amp;rsquo ; s favourite son . As it happens , there is a Leonard Cohen component , though perhaps not so much as the performers would have liked . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Part of the issue , &amp;rdquo ; says Matheson , &amp;ldquo ; was that Avery Saltzman , one of the artistic directors of the Harold Green ( and the director of this show ) , was particularly determined not to go outside the lines . He&amp;rsquo ; d say , &amp;lsquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s an incredible song , but it&amp;rsquo ; s not really a protest song . &amp;rsquo ; I love Leonard Cohen , but unfortunately a lot of his songs didn&amp;rsquo ; t fit in . But we do reference him throughout the show as one of the voices of the &amp;rsquo ; 60s. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Keeping within the lines also meant that the songwriters had to be of Jewish heritage to qualify , though , as Pitre and Matheson point out , this in no way led to a narrowing of the field . Like the Golden Age of Broadway that came before , the &amp;rsquo ; 60s boasted an astonishing abundance of Jewish songwriters and singers , especially ones who raised their voices in protest . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s an inherent sense of activism in that community , &amp;rdquo ; says Matheson . &amp;ldquo ; On the one hand they support one another , but they move that sense of activism in the community to the world at large . &amp;rdquo ; Jewish songwriters of the era , he adds , &amp;ldquo ; had a gift for expressing the difference or otherness of people in general . Which is why their songs are so universal . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;AT A GLANCE&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **27;27047;TOOLONG Times They Are A Changin ' &lt;/strong&gt; is presented from March 1 to 22 at the Segal Centre , 5170 C ? te-Ste-Catherine Rd . &lt;p&gt; Philippe Falardeau&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " https : **33;28222;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;My Salinger Year opened the 70th Berlinale&lt;/a&gt; &amp;mdash ; a.k.a. the Berlin International Film Festival &amp;mdash ; on Thursday , and no sooner had the film started than the industry trades and international media ( having viewed a press screening earlier in the day ) began posting their verdicts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;28257;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;The Guardian called it " bafflingly insipid , zestless ( and ) derivative , " &lt;/a&gt; adding that it &amp;ldquo ; clunks hard enough to smash concrete . &amp;rdquo ; Well , tell us how you really feel . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;28292;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Variety disparaged Margaret Qualley 's turn as Joanna&lt;/a&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m disappointed , &amp;rdquo ; he said , &amp;ldquo ; and I&amp;rsquo ; m not talking about the reviews , which I haven&amp;rsquo ; t read and I&amp;rsquo ; m not going to . She was like a kid yesterday . She stayed late at the party &amp;mdash ; she was one of the last to leave , talking to the crew and to everyone . That in itself is a huge gift for me. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Weaver had only good things to say Friday about her reasons for making the film , her experience making it and the end result . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I love ( my character&amp;rsquo ; s ) dry humour ; it&amp;rsquo ; s very cutting , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; She uses humour to keep people away . Alien &amp;mdash ; come on ! She&amp;rsquo ; s so graceful . One of the many things I admire about her is her ability to have this authoritative presence , and at the same time this youthful innocence and joy to her . It&amp;rsquo ; s a really awesome combination . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The relationship between the women , on and off screen , is something Falardeau believes can only help My Salinger Year . While it has been sold in many countries , the film is still looking for a U.S. distributor . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I feel we should concentrate on getting ( the film ) to the right audience , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve been receiving emails from women I don&amp;rsquo ; t know , and messages from women on Facebook . " " data-portal-copyright= " PHIL CARPENTER " **28;28957;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1728114 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You don&amp;rsquo ; t meet many people who &amp;lsquo ; kind of like&amp;rsquo ; Lhasa , &amp;rdquo ; said Mischa Karam. &amp;ldquo ; If you know about her at all , you probably love her . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lhasa de Sela had that effect on people &amp;mdash ; and through her work , she still does . The multilingual singer and songwriter , who died 10 years ago last month at age 37 , left three albums of remarkable depth and breadth &amp;mdash ; Latin American and European musical forms brought together in a singular vision , a lyrical style at once plain-spoken , poetic and mystical , all informed with a deep sense of melancholy . An adopted Montrealer , she came to be synonymous with the city that embraced her . Her presence is still felt here ; her absence still hurts . But her spirit abides. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Karam speaks from a special perspective &amp;mdash ; he is , after all , de Sela&amp;rsquo ; s brother , and now officially oversees her legacy . And as he is in a good position to know , Lhasa continues to make new friends . One of those is American writer Fred Goodman , best known for his 1997 book The Mansion on the Hill , a definitive study of the backroom managerial machinations behind some of rock&amp;rsquo ; s most iconic artists . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I heard Lhasa&amp;rsquo ; s music for the first time the week she died , &amp;rdquo ; Goodman recalled by email from his home in New York . &amp;ldquo ; I knew she was the real deal and that I had to know more about her . As I dug into her life and music , I began to feel that other Americans should be encouraged to discover her work and story . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The fruit of Goodman&amp;rsquo ; s missionary zeal is &lt;a href= " https : **33;28987;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Why Lhasa de Sela Matters&lt;/a&gt; ( University of Texas Press , 181 pages , $25.50 ) . Published in November , it&amp;rsquo ; s a slim but illuminating book that fills a gap and serves a dual purpose : the ideal introduction for Lhasa neophytes , it also offers fans entry into deeper currents of her music and sensibility . In the process , it amply justifies its title . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Her tastes and values were formed while living in a very specific bubble &amp;mdash ; one that was politically , socially and spiritually charged , &amp;rdquo ; said Goodman . &amp;ldquo ; The Kinks have a wonderful song , I&amp;rsquo ; m Not Like Everybody Else , and in their case it was a statement of aspiration . In Lhasa&amp;rsquo ; s case , it was a fact . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;29022;TOOLONG ... title= " " Lhasa had a vision of the world -- a romantic and hopeful vision that life is not simply tragic , but magic , " says biographer Fred Goodman , whose book Why Lhasa de Sela Matters was published in November . " alt= " " Lhasa had a vision of the world -- a romantic and hopeful vision that life is not simply tragic , but magic , " says biographer Fred Goodman , whose book Why Lhasa de Sela Matters was published in November . " data-portal-copyright= " Audiogram " **28;29057;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1728138 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; That uniqueness was nurtured in a peripatetic childhood that reflected the philosophy of her parents . Educator Alejandro Sela and photographer Alexandra Karam held to the ideals of the &amp;rsquo ; 60s counterculture long past the point where many gave them up . Ranging all over the United States and Alejandro&amp;rsquo ; s native Mexico in a family bus &amp;mdash ; Lhasa was born in an alternative community near Woodstock , N.Y . in 1972 &amp;mdash ; they allowed their four daughters the freedom to follow their interests . Conventional structured education was sporadic ; life education was constant . The kids were presented with a multicultural , progressive range of listening and reading options . There was no TV . Even their third daughter&amp;rsquo ; s name reflects a decidedly non-mainstream outlook . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I found ( the name ) , &amp;rdquo ; Alexandra recalled last week in the Petite-Patrie apartment where she has lived since settling in Montreal full time three years ago . &amp;ldquo ; I was reading a lot about Tibet and Buddhism at the time . I looked at this little girl&amp;rsquo ; s face , and it just felt right : Lhasa . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Was there a time when she first sensed something special in Lhasa ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;29087;TOOLONG ... title= " Lhasa , left , Ayin and Sky de Sela in Tivoli , N.Y . in 1977 . Their sister Miriam was being born in the room behind them . " alt= " Lhasa , left , Ayin and Sky de Sela in Tivoli , N.Y . in 1977 . Their sister Miriam was being born in the room behind them . " data-portal-copyright= " courtesy of Alexandra Karam " **28;29122;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1728113 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; With all those four daughters ( Mischa is her son from a subsequent marriage ) I had such absolute faith in all that I saw was within them , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; It never surprised me where they took their gifts , because they developed them so early . Lhasa was writing poems when she was five . I&amp;rsquo ; m often very critical , but Lhasa was very , very good . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A good indication of de Sela&amp;rsquo ; s precociousness , and of cultural interests hardly typical of an American child of the 1970s , was her determination at an early age that she would one day marry Victor Jara , not knowing for several years that the Chilean folksinger died a year after she was born , killed for his open defiance of the Pinochet regime . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; De Sela&amp;rsquo ; s three sisters all became circus performers . It was their training at the &amp;Eacute ; cole nationale de cirque that drew her to Montreal in 1991 , wanting to be closer to them &amp;mdash ; a move that , with hindsight , takes on the feel of destiny . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was here that she took her first tentative steps into live performance and found a crucial &lt;a href= " https : **33;29152;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;musical soulmate and mentor in guitarist Yves Desrosiers&lt;/a&gt; ; their collaboration would lead to her 1997 debut , La Llorona . A Spanish-sung album that has achieved the status of an unquestioned classic , it was also a commercial success , going platinum in Canada and selling over half a million copies worldwide . In France it made her a bona fide star . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Twelve years Lhasa&amp;rsquo ; s junior , Mischa Karam saw his half-sister only intermittently until moving to Montreal himself in 2005 . Seeing her in front of an audience for the first time was a revelation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What I remember most , &amp;rdquo ; he recalled , &amp;ldquo ; is the feeling that there was no separation between performer and audience , that everyone in the room was having this collective experience in the moment . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Having achieved a debut splash most artists could only dream of , de Sela proceeded to flout every rule of conventional career-building by joining her sisters&amp;rsquo ; one-ring travelling circus in Europe . &amp;ldquo ; She had the strength to not listen to anyone&amp;rsquo ; s advice , to go her own way , &amp;rdquo ; her mother said . &amp;ldquo ; That takes courage . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;29187;TOOLONG ... title= " Lhasa de Sela in 1998 . " There were so many different things she wanted to do , but I ca n't imagine her ever not singing , " says mother Alexandra Karam. " alt= " Lhasa de Sela in 1998 . " There were so many different things she wanted to do , but I ca n't imagine her ever not singing , " says mother Alexandra Karam. " data-portal-copyright= " RICHARD ARLESS JR . " **28;29222;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1728116 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Far from hurting her progress , this year-long interregnum served to burnish her legend : plenty of people talk figuratively of running away to join the circus , but de Sela literally did it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After folding up the circus tent , de Sela chose for a time to live in Marseille . She made her way back to Montreal by early 2003 , having abandoned sessions in France for what was to become her second and arguably best album , the Spanish/French/English collection The Living Road . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The return to the city where she had found her musical calling &amp;mdash ; a welcoming place where few thought it odd for an American-born English-speaking artist to be singing in Spanish and French &amp;mdash ; cemented Montrealers&amp;rsquo ; tendency to claim de Sela as their own . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Montreal does claim her , but that&amp;rsquo ; s fair &amp;mdash ; she claimed Montreal , too , &amp;rdquo ; said Mischa Karam. &amp;ldquo ; That first record&amp;rsquo ; s success started here , remember . And who knows &amp;mdash ; maybe it wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t have been the same in another place , where she might have been pigeonholed as &amp;lsquo ; world music&amp;rsquo ; or some other thing . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; She would have been an artist wherever she was &amp;mdash ; but a different one , &amp;rdquo ; Goodman opined. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; De Sela&amp;rsquo ; s next major artistic decision &amp;mdash ; the choice to write and record a set of songs in English &amp;mdash ; may have been at least partly down to a desire to be heard more widely in the country of her birth . The U.S. had lagged far behind Quebec and Europe in embracing her work , with sales of her first two albums there representing only a tiny percentage of their total . But that certainly wasn&amp;rsquo ; t the only reason . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; English was , after all , her first language , &amp;rdquo ; said Mischa Karam. &amp;ldquo ; She had put down roots in an English-speaking neighbourhood . She was listening to people like Al Green , Cat Power , Bonnie ( Prince ) Billy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;29252;TOOLONG ... title= " " Montreal does claim ( Lhasa de Sela ) , but that 's fair -- she claimed Montreal , too , " says brother Mischa Karam , with mother Alexandra Karam in 2015. " alt= " " Montreal does claim ( Lhasa de Sela ) , but that 's fair -- she claimed Montreal , too , " says brother Mischa Karam , with mother Alexandra Karam in 2015. " data-portal-copyright= " Stephane Bingham " **28;29287;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1728117 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; She wanted to be heard in America and had already seen how resistant the country and its gatekeepers in the media were to her French and Spanish songs , &amp;rdquo ; Goodman said . &amp;ldquo ; She made that record ( 2009&amp;rsquo ; s eponymous Lhasa ) with America in mind . And it&amp;rsquo ; s not something that kowtows to American tastes . Quite the opposite . It&amp;rsquo ; s extremely personal and defies commercial expectations . She simply offered American listeners a version of herself that they could understand . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was at this time , seemingly the most happy and settled in her life &amp;mdash ; she bought a house on Esplanade Ave . in Mile End and embarked on a relationship with local mastering engineer Ryan Morey &amp;mdash ; that de Sela got sick . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The breast cancer that was to claim her life went undetected in an early misdiagnosis , causing a crucial near-two years of possible treatment to be lost . By the time the cancer was identified , said her mother , &amp;ldquo ; it was too late . &amp;rdquo ; Lhasa de Sela died on New Year&amp;rsquo ; s Day , 2010 . Many Montrealers still recall that her passing was followed by four straight days of heavy snow . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While it&amp;rsquo ; s impossible to know what de Sela would be doing were she still alive , educated guesses can be made . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think she wanted to make more music , and at a quicker pace than what she had been used to , &amp;rdquo ; Mischa Karam said . &amp;ldquo ; The seven years between albums , with a circus or an existential crisis or maybe both in between , that sense of moulting and regenerating &amp;hellip ; I think she wanted less of that . She talked about building a studio and rehearsal space of her own , improvising more , collaborating more . She mentioned people like Godspeed You ! Black Emperor . She was planning an album of covers of Victor Jara and Violeta Parra songs . She was writing a book . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One of the really sad things about the timing of her death is that she was ready to open herself to the community where she was putting down roots , and go into things with a little less control , just to see what happened . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There were so many different things she wanted to do , but I can&amp;rsquo ; t imagine her ever not singing , &amp;rdquo ; said Alexandra Karam. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thoughts of what might have been are channelled by Goodman in an unexpected touch . He ends his written account of de Sela&amp;rsquo ; s life and work with The Girl-Fish , a brief Catalonian folk tale on the theme of regeneration . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Lhasa had a vision of the world &amp;mdash ; a romantic and hopeful vision that life is not simply tragic , but magic , &amp;rdquo ; said Goodman . &amp;ldquo ; I added the folk tale as a postscript in the belief that she would prefer her romantic and mystical vision of life to stand as the last word . As Lhasa said in one of her songs , &amp;lsquo ; There is no end to this story . &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Regeneration and its implicit faith in the future brings us back to Alexandra Karam&amp;rsquo ; s belief in her children&amp;rsquo ; s gifts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In fact , I feel that way about children , period , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; If they&amp;rsquo ; re given the opportunity and the space to develop what really interests them , what they love , they&amp;rsquo ; re going to do amazing things . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In that light , it&amp;rsquo ; s all the more poignant to consider Parc Lhasa-De Sela , the little urban oasis at the northern edge of Mile End that was officially dedicated in her name in 2014. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s my favourite park in the neighbourhood for young kids , &amp;rdquo ; said Montreal writer Saleema Nawaz , mother of a five-year-old . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s totally self-contained and it has everything you want : play structures , swings , a sandbox , green space , a hill , picnic tables , a splash pad . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some of those children are bound to be curious , and to ask their parents about this Lhasa person whose name this welcoming space bears . And the legend will continue to grow . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;29317;TOOLONG ... title= " Lhasa de Sela and mother Alexandra Karam in 2000 .
